title: batch: fix dep_add_blocker directional footgun (canonical id/blocker schema, loud validation, unified dep path)
description:
Context: on 2026-07-13 a batch dep_add_blocker call created a REVERSED dependency. The op name uses blocker vocabulary, the fields use parent/child family vocabulary, and the house genesis-bead convention reads parent as the BLOCKED umbrella (children block the genesis) - the inverse of batch.rs where parent blocks child. The mistake was invisible: unknown extra JSON fields are silently ignored, and success output is a mute op-ok.

Scope (src/batch.rs, cli help, tests):
1. Canonical schema: dep_add_blocker takes id (the bead being blocked) and blocker (must close before id becomes ready). Keep parent and child as serde ALIASES mapping parent to blocker and child to id, so every existing caller is preserved exactly (parent=X child=Y still yields X blocks Y). Add a compat test proving alias equivalence.
2. Loud misuse: pre-validate each op object keys against an allowlist via a serde_json Value pass before the typed parse (serde deny_unknown_fields does not work with internally tagged enums). Unknown keys are an error naming the offending key and the allowed set. Success output echoes the edge in words, e.g. ok: X blocked by Y, in text mode; json mode may add fields but must not change existing ones (br output parity per repo CLAUDE.md).
3. Unify code paths: route execute_dep_add_blocker through the same function the dep add CLI command uses so validation (cycle detection, duplicate-edge handling) cannot diverge. Direction-parity test: dep add A B and batch with id=A blocker=B produce identical dependencies rows. Ready-set test: blocked bead absent from ready until blocker closes.
4. Docs: br batch --help prints per-op field schemas with one worked example each, including the direction sentence for dep_add_blocker.

Constraints: bf is a strict br superset - no existing flag or output format may change shape. cargo build clean; tests pass. Do not refactor beyond the stated scope.

Deployment note: this must not strand unreleased on main - the deployed fleet binary is 0.2.0 and already missing months of fixes. If a release/deploy bead exists in this workspace, add this fix to it and reference it in the close comment; if none exists, say so loudly in the close comment so the operator cuts a release.
close_reason: Implemented in commit 8b5c41b6. Fixed dep_add_blocker directional footgun with: (1) canonical id/blocker schema with parent/child aliases, (2) loud field validation with clear error messages, (3) unified execute_dep_add_blocker() with cycle/duplicate detection, (4) enhanced br batch --help with per-op schemas. All 137 tests pass. DEPLOYMENT NOTE: NO release/deploy bead exists in workspace - OPERATOR MUST CUT A RELEASE to deploy this fix (fleet binary is 0.2.0, months behind).

title: Investigate bf ready returning zero results despite open-status beads
description:
Observed live 2026-07-20 in this repo's own .beads workspace: 'bf list --format json' shows 54 beads with status=open (out of 899 total: 631 closed, 163 blocked, 44 in_progress, 5 completed, 1 done, 54 open). 'bf ready --limit 500 --json' returns an empty array — zero beads, not a subset. Either every one of those 54 open beads genuinely has an unresolved blocker (plausible but unverified — some of the open beads sampled, e.g. bf-s9tt7 'Test epic creation', bf-127ow 'Test Epic 1', look like standalone test-created beads unlikely to have real dependencies), or bf ready's query has a correctness bug (e.g. treating a bead as blocked by something that isn't actually unclosed, or a bug specific to the primary/multi-workspace claim path noted in fix(claim): claim_ttl_minutes commit 99f68beb).

Pick a handful of the 54 open beads (bf list --status open --format json), run 'bf show <id>' or inspect their dependency rows directly, and confirm by hand whether they have a genuinely unclosed blocker. If any have none, that's a confirmed bf ready bug — find and fix the query in the ready-computation code path (search src/ for the ready-set query, likely near or shared with the claim query in src/claim.rs) and add a regression test: an open bead with zero dependencies must appear in bf ready output.

title: target/ build directory (18,598 files) tracked in git -- no top-level .gitignore exists
description:
The bead-forge repo root has no `.gitignore` file at all (only `.beads/.gitignore` exists, which only covers `.beads/` contents). As a result `cargo build`'s entire `target/` directory is tracked in git:

    git ls-files | grep '^target/' | wc -l   # => 18598

This causes every `cargo build` to generate a massive noisy `git status`/`git diff` (observed firsthand: a routine `git status` on this checkout produced 18k+ lines of target/ fingerprint/build-script noise -- deleted-file entries, .rustc_info.json, .cargo-lock, etc. -- burying real changes like the doctor.rs debug print in bead bf-forge-doctor-debug). It also bloats git history/clone size with rebuildable binary artifacts.

Acceptance criteria:
- Add a top-level .gitignore excluding /target, Cargo build artifacts, and common editor/OS cruft.
- git rm -r --cached target/ to untrack all 18598 currently-tracked build artifacts (keep them on disk).
- Confirm `git status` is clean/minimal after a fresh `cargo build`.
close_reason: Implemented: added .gitignore excluding /target/, removed 3,596 tracked build artifacts from git. Clean git status after cargo build. Committed 7a878c40.

title: Add checksum verification to bf-update.sh before installing downloaded binary
description:
deploy/bf-update.sh (and the NixOS-variant scripts/bf-update.sh) download bf-linux-x86_64 from the GitHub Releases API and install it straight to ~/.local/bin/bf with zero integrity verification, running unattended hourly via bf-update.timer across every fleet host (Hetzner confirmed active; lab and kalshi-interserver VPS pending per docs/deploy/ROLLOUT.md). Any MITM on the download, or a compromised/corrupted GitHub release asset, gets installed and executed fleet-wide with no check.

Fix: have the bead-forge-build CI workflow (WorkflowTemplate 'bead-forge-build' in iad-ci) publish a SHA256SUMS file alongside bf-linux-x86_64 in each GitHub release, and have bf-update.sh download it and verify the binary's checksum before chmod+mv into place. Fail loudly (non-zero exit, clear log line) and leave the old binary in place if verification fails. Apply to both deploy/bf-update.sh and the NixOS variant referenced from systemd/README.md.

title: 7.1 Incremental auto-flush + dirty_issues tracking
description: Spec: docs/plan/plan.md Phase 7.1 (P0). Amends Core Principle 2. Add dirty_issues table (issue_id, marked_at); every mutation marks dirty. After each successful mutation, best-effort incremental export of dirty rows only into issues.jsonl (surgical line replacement, not full rewrite); on failure warn on stderr + warning field in --json envelope, keep dirty marks, never fail the mutation. Recovery: bf sync --flush-only clears dirty set. Config sync.auto_flush default true; --no-auto-flush override. bf batch flushes ONCE at transaction end. Read-only/diagnostic commands must never write JSONL. Exit criteria: kill a worker between mutation and flush and lose nothing; flush failure visible in machine-readable output; flush-before-repair ritual becomes unnecessary. comments.author: cli
comments.text:
7.1 Open Question RESOLVED — rotation interplay: incremental auto-flush targets ONLY the active issues.jsonl and NEVER rotated archives (issues.jsonl.1/.2/…).

Code path (single resolution site, by construction):
- Auto-flush entrypoint src/autoflush.rs::after_mutation -> run() -> crate::sync::flush_dirty (autoflush.rs:71-73). Hard-delete variant after_delete -> flush_after_delete.
- src/sync.rs::flush_dirty (sync.rs:98) resolves the export target in exactly ONE place: `let jsonl_path = beads_dir.join(&metadata.jsonl_export);` (sync.rs:104) -> the active issues.jsonl. It hands that path to export_jsonl_dirty.
- src/jsonl.rs::export_jsonl_dirty (jsonl.rs:188) -> export_jsonl_merge(path, &issues, &[]) (jsonl.rs:202). export_jsonl_merge (jsonl.rs:104) reads/writes only the path it is given, via atomic temp+rename, and never enumerates or opens numbered archives. Archives are written EXCLUSIVELY by crate::rotate::rotate.

Because the active path is the sole resolution on this path, an archive path is never constructed here — the guarantee holds by construction, with no runtime guard needed. (Doc comments on flush_dirty and export_jsonl_dirty already record this as RESOLVED.)

Confirming tests (both pass):
- tests/autoflush_diagnostics_and_rotation.rs::autoflush_targets_only_active_jsonl_not_archives (line 217): workspace with a hand-written issues.jsonl.1 archive (closed bead) is mutated via `bf update` (auto-flush); asserts the active file changes in content AND mtime while the archive stays byte-for-byte identical with unchanged mtime, and that the mutated bead did not leak into the archive.
- tests/batch_cascade_and_rotation.rs::incremental_flush_targets_only_active_jsonl_not_archive (line 182): same invariant from the batch path.

No code change required for this resolution — behavior is already correct and tested. Closes plan §7.1 Open question (docs/plan/plan.md:1389-1390).

title: bf ready --format json omits assignee and labels fields, silently breaking downstream candidate filtering
description:
Confirmed directly: bf ready --limit 10 --format json against a bead known (via bf show) to have both a real assignee (claude-code-glm-4.7-alpha) and a label (split-child) returns JSON with no assignee key and no labels key at all -- only id, title, status, priority, downstream_impact, critical_float, created_at.

IMPACT: any consumer that deserializes bf ready --json into a struct with optional assignee/labels fields will silently see them as empty/None regardless of the bead true state, since the JSON simply omits them rather than reporting null or an empty value. Confirmed this is the direct root cause of a NEEDLE fleet-wide stall (see companion bead filed in NEEDLE): explore strand relies on assignee and labels from this exact JSON shape to filter out already-claimed or excluded-label beads, and cannot do so correctly because the data was never in the response to begin with.

This is distinct from the already-filed bead about bf update not being able to clear an assignee (that one is about mutation; this one is about the ready command output schema being incomplete).

ACCEPTANCE:
- bf ready --format json includes assignee (null when unset) and labels (empty array when none) for every returned bead, matching what bf show already reports for the same bead.
- Regression test: a bead with a real assignee and a label appears in bf ready --json output (since ready does not filter on assignee/labels itself, per its own docs) WITH those fields populated, not omitted.
- Audit bf list/bf search --format json for the same gap while in this area -- worth checking whether they have the identical omission.

title: Use authenticated GitHub API requests in bf-update.sh to avoid rate-limit flakiness
description:
deploy/bf-update.sh calls the GitHub REST API for the bead-forge repo's latest release, unauthenticated, twice per invocation (once for the tag_name check, once for the asset download URL), on an hourly systemd timer across every fleet host sharing this server's egress IP. Unauthenticated GitHub API rate limit is 60 requests/hour per source IP, shared with any other unauthenticated GitHub API usage from the same host/IP. Currently under budget with 1 host active, but docs/deploy/ROLLOUT.md plans 2 more hosts (lab, kalshi-interserver VPS) plus ad hoc manual runs, and this script is documented as a copyable template for other repos' auto-update timers.

Fix: have bf-update.sh use a GITHUB_TOKEN if present in the environment or a configurable token file (e.g. under ~/.config/bf-update/), passing it as a curl Authorization header, which raises the limit to 5000/hour. Fall back to unauthenticated if no token is configured so the script keeps working with zero setup. Document the optional token file in deploy/README.md.

title: Add previous-binary backup and rollback to bf-update.sh
description:
deploy/bf-update.sh overwrites ~/.local/bin/bf directly on every successful download (mv "$TEMP_DIR/bf-linux-x86_64" "$BIN_DIR/bf") with no backup of the binary being replaced. Because this runs unattended hourly across the fleet (see docs/deployment.md fleet table), a bad release (crash-on-launch, broken CLI flag parsing, etc.) breaks bf on every host within an hour with no fast way back — every NEEDLE worker and human on that host loses bf until a fixed release ships.

Fix: before the mv, copy the current /bf to /bf.previous (and record its version in .bf-version.previous). Add a --rollback flag to bf-update.sh (or a small bf-rollback.sh alongside it) that restores bf.previous -> bf and the matching .bf-version. Document the rollback step in docs/deployment.md's 'Manual update' section.

title: Wire auto-flush into batch, claim, delete, and mitosis with single end-of-transaction flush
description:
Phase 7.1 (parent bf-1wg2v) auto-split child 3/5. Depends on child 2.

Scope — the mutation paths that are NOT simple single-issue updates:
1. bf batch (cmd_batch src/cli/mod.rs:1939 -> src/batch.rs execute_batch) and cmd_mitosis (:1983): flush ONCE at transaction end, not per-op (avoid write amplification). The autoflush module already exposes a batch path (src/autoflush.rs tests cover batch) — call it exactly once after execute_batch commits.
2. cmd_claim (:1484 -> src/claim.rs): flush after the claim transaction commits; surface warning via child-1 channel.
3. cmd_delete (:1425): currently runs `tx.execute("DELETE FROM issues ...")` with NO dirty mark — it relies on FK CASCADE, which silently drops the dirty_issues row, so a deleted bead never reaches JSONL. Fix so deletion is reflected: mark dirty (or explicitly remove the JSONL line) so the next flush removes it from issues.jsonl.

Acceptance criteria (tempdir tests):
- A batch with N ops triggers EXACTLY ONE JSONL write (assert multiplicity, e.g. mtime changes once or a write spy counter == 1).
- claim writes the claimed bead's new state to JSONL; flush failure surfaces a warning without failing the claim.
- delete removes the bead's line from issues.jsonl (no orphan line remains after flush).
- mitosis flushes once.
- cargo build clean; tests pass.
close_reason: Verified the single-end-of-transaction auto-flush wiring on the four non-single-issue mutation paths. cmd_batch/cmd_mitosis (src/cli/mod.rs) call autoflush_after_mutation exactly once after execute_batch commits; cmd_claim flushes after the claim txn and surfaces a warning on flush failure without failing the claim; cmd_delete uses autoflush_after_delete to prune the removed id (the FK-cascade orphan fix). src/batch.rs marks every touched bead dirty via mark_dirty_tx within the batch txn, so one flush exports them all — no per-op write amplification. Added tests/autoflush_batch_claim_delete.rs (8 tempdir tests covering all four acceptance criteria: batch=N ops -> one write, claim state + failure-warns-without-failing, delete prunes orphan, mitosis flushes once). cargo build clean; cargo test --test autoflush_batch_claim_delete = 8 passed. Committed fb3edd3 and pushed.

title: .beads/.gitignore *.db pattern misses beads.db.backup.* -- 9 SQLite binaries committed to git
description:
src/doctor.rs:395-400 backs up the live database before repair using:
    let backup_path = db_path.with_extension(&format!("db.backup.{}", <timestamp>));
    std::fs::copy(&db_path, &backup_path)?;

producing filenames like `beads.db.backup.20260624144845`. `.beads/.gitignore` only excludes `*.db`, `*.db-journal`, `*.db-shm`, `*.db-wal` -- none of which match `*.db.backup.*`. As a result, 9 binary SQLite backup files (confirmed via `git ls-files | grep beads.db.backup`, ~483-495KB each, ~4.3MB total) are committed to the bead-forge git history.

This directly contradicts the plan's own design decision #12 (docs/plan/plan.md): "`beads.db` is gitignored (binary, rebuilt from JSONL on `bf sync --import`)".

Acceptance criteria:
- Add `*.db.backup.*` (or `beads.db.backup.*`) to .beads/.gitignore.
- git rm --cached the 9 existing tracked backup files (git ls-files | grep 'beads.db.backup') so they stop being tracked.
- Verify a fresh `bf doctor --repair` no longer produces an untracked-but-wanted file, i.e. confirm the new gitignore pattern actually matches doctor.rs's naming scheme.
close_reason: Added *.db.backup.* to .beads/.gitignore (matched doctor.rs backup pattern). Removed 28 tracked SQLite backups (~4.3MB) from git. Verified new backup files are now ignored. Commit cbcda305 pushed to origin.

title: bf reopen must clear the assignee field
description:
Part of bf-gj673 — see docs/plan/plan.md section 3.4.

cmd_reopen (src/cli/mod.rs ~line 1362-1375) builds an IssueChanges with only status: Some(Status::Open) set, everything else defaulted. IssueChanges::assignee defaults to None, which update_issue's merge logic treats as 'do not touch this field' — so bf reopen never clears the assignee. A bead reopened after being closed/tombstoned keeps whatever assignee it had, even though it's now logically unclaimed.

This is a confirmed real-world root cause: on the lab NEEDLE fleet audit (2026-07-21), beads reopened by tooling ended up status=open with a stale foreign assignee still set — a state that permanently excluded them from NEEDLE's roaming-worker candidate discovery (any bead with a non-empty assignee is treated as already-claimed, regardless of status), with no self-healing path (NEEDLE's mend strand only reclaims in_progress beads, not open ones with a leftover assignee).

Fix: cmd_reopen should explicitly clear the assignee by setting assignee to an empty string in the IssueChanges it builds (relies on the empty-string-clears-to-NULL fix from the sibling bead bf-4mj7l).

Note: this bead is naturally sequenced after (or alongside) the sibling CLI-validation-removal bead — verify the fix lands correctly regardless of implementation order, and add a regression test.

Acceptance criteria:
- bf reopen on a bead with an existing assignee results in assignee being cleared (verified via bf show)
- bf reopen on a bead with no assignee still works (no-op on assignee, no error)
- Add a test in tests/ (new or existing reopen test file) covering: reopen clears a previously-set assignee
- cargo build clean, cargo clippy all-targets -D warnings clean, cargo fmt applied
close_reason: bf reopen now clears the assignee: cmd_reopen (src/cli/mod.rs:1581) builds IssueChanges with assignee: Some(String::new()), and update_issue's storage layer (src/storage/sqlite.rs:545) maps the empty string to assignee = NULL — never persisting a literal empty string that would read back as 'assigned' and hide the bead from claiming. Reopening is thus logically unclaimed again (fixes the NEEDLE fleet-audit state where reopened beads kept a stale foreign assignee). The fix (fe50a54) and regression tests (16ab5b4: test_reopen_clears_assignee + test_reopen_without_assignee_is_noop in tests/test_close_reopen_integration.rs) were already committed; this pass re-verified: cargo build clean, both reopen regression tests pass (7/7 in the file), and the bead's own files are fmt-clean. Notes committed in 33fc93b and pushed. All on origin/main.

title: 7.1e Exit-criteria integration test: kill a worker between mutation and flush loses nothing
description:
Parent: bf-1wg2v (Phase 7.1, split child 5 of 5 — LAST child, blocks the umbrella). Depends on bf-3a4hk. Spec: docs/plan/plan.md §7.1 Exit criteria.

FOCUS: the headline proof that 7.1 is done. The first two clauses are this child; the third was proven in child 3.

Scope — a tempdir-only integration test (per plan Test Strategy) that simulates the catastrophic case the whole feature exists to prevent:
- Perform a mutation (e.g. create + claim) where the db commit lands but the auto-flush is interrupted (simulate a worker killed mid-flush: perform the mutation with auto-flush disabled or interrupt the flush, leaving the bead dirty-only in the db).
- Assert the bead is recoverable: running 'bf sync --flush-only' exports it into issues.jsonl, and 'git diff .beads/issues.jsonl' (or equivalent line check) shows the change.
- Assert that a 'bf doctor --repair' performed WHILE beads are dirty-but-unflushed does NOT silently lose them (doctor.rs already has dirty-preservation; assert it holds here end-to-end). This is the 2026-06-10 wipe regression class — the test must guard it.
- Final clause: assert a flush failure is visible in machine-readable output (re-assert child 3's --json warning in the full end-to-end path, or reference that test).

Acceptance criteria:
- The kill-a-worker scenario test passes in a tempdir and fails if auto-flush/dirty-tracking is removed or disabled (i.e. it is a real guard, not a tautology).
- Document in a comment that, with this test green, the 'flush before repair' ritual in ~/bead-forge CLAUDE.md is no longer load-bearing for data safety (do NOT edit CLAUDE.md in this child — note it for the umbrella close).
- cargo build + cargo test clean. This child closing unblocks the umbrella (bf-1wg2v).

title: 7.1c Surface flush failures via stderr + --json warning envelope (never fail mutation)
description:
Parent: bf-1wg2v (Phase 7.1, split child 3 of 5). Depends on bf-2rjhk (CLI wiring in place). Spec: docs/plan/plan.md §7.1.

FOCUS: the failure contract. 'on failure: warn loudly (stderr + warning field in the --json envelope), keep the dirty marks, never fail the mutation.' Child 2 swallowed autoflush errors; this child makes them VISIBLE in machine-readable output while still never failing the mutation.

Scope:
- When autoflush::run returns Err (or exports 0 of N dirty rows in a way that indicates partial failure), capture the error string.
- Stderr: print a clear, prefixed warning line (e.g. 'warning: auto-flush failed: <reason>; run "bf sync --flush-only" to retry'). Goes to stderr only, never stdout, so it never corrupts --json pipes.
- --json envelope: add a 'warning' field (string or null) to the JSON output of mutation commands when a flush failed. Define ONE stable shape for the warning field (consistent across all mutation commands) so agent consumers can detect it uniformly.
- Keep dirty marks on failure (do not clear dirty_issues) so the next mutation / 'bf sync --flush-only' retries. Verify the dirty row survives a failed flush.

Acceptance criteria:
- Tempdir test that forces a flush failure (e.g. make issues.jsonl unwritable / dir read-only, or inject a corrupt line) and asserts: (a) 'bf create --json' still SUCCEEDS (exit 0, bead created in db); (b) the JSON carries a non-null 'warning' field; (c) the bead stays in dirty_issues; (d) 'bf sync --flush-only' after the dir is made writable clears it.
- Manual/automated check that the warning is on stderr, not stdout (so 'bf create --json | jq .' still parses).
- cargo build + cargo test clean.
close_reason: Failure contract for auto-flush (Phase 7.1 child 3/5): a failed flush now degrades to a VISIBLE warning instead of being swallowed, while the mutation still succeeds. Single-source message flush_failed_warning() in src/autoflush.rs (used by after_mutation + after_delete) embeds the recovery cmd on BOTH channels: stderr 'warning: auto-flush to JSONL failed: <err>; run "bf sync --flush-only" to retry' and the --json envelope's top-level non-null string 'warning' key (absent on the clean path). src/format/warning.rs documents the ONE stable shape and provides with_warning()/warn_stderr() (warning never written to stdout, so 'bf create --json | jq .' always parses). Dirty marks retained on failure (clear_dirty only after a successful export) so the next mutation or 'bf sync --flush-only' recovers. Verified: cargo build clean; autoflush_failure_contract 3/3 (forces flush failure via wedged issues.jsonl dir, asserts exit 0 + bead in db + non-null warning + stderr-only line + dirty retention + recovery flush); format::warning unit tests 4/4; sister autoflush suites (mutation/wiring/batch_claim_delete/readonly) compile+run clean. Committed in 02374fa and confirmed on origin/needle/bf-5wku.

title: Implement ADR-1: bf-checkpoint auto-flush/commit timer for .beads/ workspaces
description:
Implements the decision recorded in docs/plan/plan.md, section 'ADR-1: 2026-07-20 - Automatic periodic checkpointing of .beads/ git state'.

Scope:
1. bf-checkpoint.sh (deploy/ and systemd/ variants, mirroring the existing bf-update.sh split) that: runs 'bf sync --flush-only' for a configured workspace, checks 'git diff --quiet -- .beads/issues.jsonl', and if changed, stages ONLY .beads/issues.jsonl (never beads.db) and commits with git identity user.email=github@jedarden.com / user.name=jedarden and message prefix 'chore(beads): auto-checkpoint'.
2. Push stays opt-in: a --push flag, off by default.
3. New '.beads/config.yaml' block: 'checkpoint: { enabled: bool (default false), interval_minutes: int, push: bool (default false) }' — parse it in src/config.rs alongside the existing scoring/rotate/secret_protection blocks.
4. systemd unit pair (bf-checkpoint.service/.timer) deployed the same way bf-update.timer already is, per docs/deploy/README.md and docs/deploy/ROLLOUT.md conventions.
5. Do NOT touch src/claim.rs or any hot claim/close path — checkpointing must stay out-of-band per ADR-1's consequences.
6. Update docs/deployment.md and docs/deploy/README.md with the new mechanism, defaulting new rollouts to checkpoint.enabled=false until a maintainer opts a workspace in.

The storage layer (src/storage/sqlite.rs ~line 545-554) already correctly converts an empty/whitespace assignee into 'assignee = NULL' — this CLI guard is the only thing blocking that path from ever being reached. bf update <id> --assignee '' must succeed and clear the assignee.

3. src/validation.rs's validate_assignee() function: given its current callers are both being removed, either delete it (and its now-uncalled unit tests) or repurpose it into a pure normalization helper (Option str to Option String, trimming and collapsing empty to None) called from both cmd_create and cmd_update, so the logic isn't duplicated. 4. tests/test_assignee_validation.rs: six tests are currently marked ignore, with the reason 'aspirational: assignee validation never implemented; empty assignee now means clear/unassigned (br parity) - revisit via tracking bead'. title: close_issue() never transitions a dependent's status from blocked to open when its last blocker closes
description:
`bf close <id>` (and `bf batch close`, which calls the same path) leaves every dependent bead permanently stuck at status='blocked' even after its last real blocker closes. This silently freezes any sequential dependency chain (genesis + phase beads, the documented convention in this environment's CLAUDE.md) after the very first phase closes -- `bf ready` never surfaces the next phase again without manual intervention.

## Root cause

`close_issue()` in src/storage/sqlite.rs:671-717. After the UPDATE that sets the just-closed bead's own status to 'closed', the function only does:

```rust
// Invalidate critical path cache: closing a bead can unblock dependents
invalidate_cache(tx)?;
compute_all_critical_paths(tx)?;
```

The comment correctly identifies that closing a bead can unblock dependents, but the code only recomputes the critical_path_cache (ES/LS/float scheduling metadata) -- it never calls rebuild_blocked_cache(), and critically it never touches the `status` column of any OTHER bead. `bf ready` filters strictly on `issues.status = 'open'` (see idx_issues_ready), so a dependent bead created while its blocker was still open keeps status='blocked' forever, even once genuinely unblocked, unless someone runs `bf update <id> --status open` by hand.

Distinct from bf-wre (which fixed rebuild_blocked_cache()'s terminal-status recognition -- a read-side query correctness bug) and bf-1ak (which fixed dependency *direction* at creation time). Neither touches the write-side cascade this bug is about. Confirmed via direct reproduction in jedarden/twitterapi-proxy on 2026-07-15: closing Phase 1 left Phase 2 at status='blocked' with blocked_issues_cache correctly empty (proving the cache-vs-status split is the actual failure mode, not a cache staleness issue) -- and the same thing recurred closing Phase 2, leaving Phase 3 stuck, confirming it's not a one-off.

## Acceptance criteria

- In close_issue() (and any other write path that closes/completes a bead, e.g. bf-wre's TERMINAL_STATUS_ALIASES-aware paths), after closing `id`: find every bead Y with a dependency row (Y depends_on id, type in the same set rebuild_blocked_cache() already uses: 'blocks', 'parent-child', 'conditional-blocks', 'waits-for'). For each Y currently at status='blocked' (do not touch any other status -- in_progress, deferred, or any custom status a human explicitly set must be left alone), check whether Y has any OTHER remaining blocker not in TERMINAL_STATUS_SQL_LIST. If none, transition Y's status to 'open' in the same transaction.
- Call rebuild_blocked_cache() in the same transaction so blocked_issues_cache stays consistent with the status change, closing the same class of staleness bf-wre addressed for the read side.
- Add a regression test mirroring bf-wre's style: create bead A, bead B blocked by A (status='blocked' at creation), close A, assert B.status == Status::Open and B does not appear in blocked_issues_cache. Also test the negative case: bead C blocked by both A and D (D still open) -- closing A must NOT open C.
- Add a `bf doctor` check (mirroring bf-wre's pseudo_terminal_status_ids check) that finds beads currently sitting at status='blocked' with zero non-terminal blockers remaining -- this bug has likely left stale 'blocked' beads scattered across every repo in the lab NEEDLE fleet that uses sequential phase-bead chains (the genesis-bead convention in CLAUDE.md), the same way bf-wre found 106 pre-existing affected beads at scale. Surface count + repo breakdown like bf-wre's doctor check did, so those can be swept with `bf update --status open` without a manual per-repo sqlite query.
- Verify against beads_rust (canonical br) behavior per this repo's CLAUDE.md output-parity requirement before deciding whether this is a bf-only enhancement or something to also flag upstream.
close_reason: Implemented blocked->open status cascade on close. The close_issue() function now transitions dependent beads from 'blocked' to 'open' when their last blocker closes. Includes: (1) Core cascade logic in src/storage/sqlite.rs:779-832, (2) Doctor check in src/doctor.rs for detecting stale blocked beads, (3) Comprehensive test coverage in tests/test_bf_5id.rs and tests/test_blocked_cascade.rs. All tests pass. cargo build clean.

comments.author: cli
comments.text: ROOT CAUSE (bf-um3e correlation): The capital-E 'Error:' prefix is NOT clap and NOT bead-forge code — it is the Rust std Termination impl for Result<T,E:Debug>. main() is 'fn main() -> Result<()>' and propagates errors via '?'; on Err the runtime prints 'Error: {:?}' to stderr and exits 1. That is why grepping src/ only found the unrelated format_error literals (text.rs:41, toon.rs:40) — the real source lives in std, out-of-tree. Verified empirically: 'bf show <missing>' -> 'Error: Bead not found' on stderr exit 1; 'bf bogus' -> lowercase clap 'error:' exit 2; 'bf --version' -> clean 'bf 0.3.0' stdout exit 0 (never reaches Error: path). Classification: EXPECTED behavior, not a bug, not config. Minor note: errors propagated via '?' bypass the selected --format formatter, so '--format json' failures still print plain-text 'Error: ...'. Full writeup: notes/bf-um3e.md

title: Add interval throttle, opt-in push, and deploy/scripts parity check to bf-checkpoint.sh
description:
Split slice #4 (FINAL) of parent bf-3cu1k (ADR-1 bf-checkpoint.sh). Depends on child bf-61nxm (commit/identity). The script already exists and is committed (fef0340) in deploy/ and scripts/. This child OWNS and VERIFIES the throttle, the opt-in push, and the final deploy/scripts parity — and is the LAST child the umbrella parent waits on. Do NOT touch src/claim.rs or any claim/close hot path.

Scope (this slice only):
- Per-workspace self-throttle on checkpoint.interval_minutes via a per-workspace state file under ${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/bf-checkpoint/<workspace-slug>.last; if the last checkpoint was less than interval_minutes ago, skip (print message, exit 0). Write the timestamp after a successful checkpoint (and on the no-op no-change path).
- --push is OFF by default. `git push` runs ONLY when --push is passed OR persistent checkpoint.push=true. Default behavior (neither) does NOT push.
- Variant PARITY: scripts/bf-checkpoint.sh (NixOS) is bit-identical to deploy/bf-checkpoint.sh EXCEPT the shebang and the single descriptive comment naming which variant it is — exactly mirroring the bf-update.sh split.

Acceptance:
- Two runs within interval_minutes: the second skips with a throttle message and exit 0.
- With no --push and checkpoint.push=false (default), the script commits but does NOT run `git push`.
- With --push (or checkpoint.push=true) it runs `git push` after committing.
- `diff deploy/bf-checkpoint.sh scripts/bf-checkpoint.sh` shows ONLY the shebang line and the one variant-description comment differ.
- `bash -n` passes on BOTH variants; shellcheck clean IF shellcheck is installed (note: not installed on this box — record that it was skipped, do not block on it).
- src/claim.rs and any hot path UNTOUCHED.
close_reason: Slice #4 (FINAL) of bf-3cu1k, re-verified on retry (failure-count:1). Runtime logic (per-workspace interval throttle via XDG_STATE_HOME/bf-checkpoint/<slug>.last checked before flush; opt-in --push / checkpoint.push, OFF by default) was already correct from fef0340; only source change was d8712fb collapsing the variant comment so parity is unambiguous. Independent /tmp harness (/tmp/cp-verify.sh, isolated workspaces + bare remote): 20/20 PASS on deploy/ AND 20/20 on scripts/ (exit 0). Throttle: pre-seeded state skips BEFORE flush (no Flushing line); 2nd run within interval_minutes exits 0 with 'skipping' and no new commit. Push OFF: commits, no 'Pushing' line, remote unchanged. Push ON via --push AND via config push=true: 'Pushing' line, remote gains commit. diff shows exactly the 2 allowed hunks (shebang + one variant comment), mirroring bf-update.sh; bash -n clean both; shellcheck skipped (not installed, acceptance allows). Env correction: box IS NixOS (no /bin/bash), so scripts/ is native; deploy shebang untestable here but parity diff suffices. src/claim.rs and hot path untouched (d8712fb touched no src/; claim.rs clean). notes/bf-5y3cj.md; pushed e19317f on needle/bf-5wku.

title: bf close crashes on non-RFC3339 claimed_at from claim.rs worker_sessions insert
description:
`bf close <id>` can hard-fail with `Error: Invalid claimed_at format: premature end of input`, permanently preventing that bead from being closed via bf close.

Root cause: two divergent code paths insert into `worker_sessions`:
- src/storage/sqlite.rs `record_worker_session()` (~line 1487) explicitly sets `claimed_at = now.to_rfc3339()` -- correct RFC3339.
- src/claim.rs (two `INSERT INTO worker_sessions` statements, ~line 265 and ~line 354, inside the claim() transaction) omit `claimed_at` from the column list entirely, so it falls back to the schema default `DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` (src/storage/schema.rs:275). SQLite's CURRENT_TIMESTAMP produces `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` (no 'T', no offset) -- NOT RFC3339.

`update_session_on_close()` in src/velocity.rs:95-97 does `DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339(&claimed_at_str)` with `?` propagation -- any session row created via the claim.rs path fails to parse and aborts the entire close operation.

Evidence this already happened in production: notes/bf-2j9e.md documents `bf close bf-2j9e` failing with exactly this error after a successful flush, forcing the bead to be abandoned/retried instead of closed. tmp_fix_worker_sessions.py (repo root) is a hand-written one-off script that manually DELETEd "malformed" worker_sessions rows with empty claimed_at for bead bf-1leo to work around the same class of bug.

Acceptance criteria:
- src/claim.rs's two `INSERT INTO worker_sessions` statements explicitly set `claimed_at` to `Utc::now().to_rfc3339()` (matching sqlite.rs's record_worker_session), instead of relying on the CURRENT_TIMESTAMP default.
- src/velocity.rs's `update_session_on_close()` parses claimed_at defensively (accept both RFC3339 and SQLite's native DATETIME format, or skip/warn on a malformed row instead of erroring the whole close) so one bad historical row can never block bf close again.
- Add a regression test that inserts a worker_sessions row with a non-RFC3339 claimed_at (SQLite CURRENT_TIMESTAMP style) and asserts `bf close` on that bead still succeeds.
- Remove tmp_fix_worker_sessions.py from repo root once the root cause is fixed in code.
close_reason: Fixed: claim.rs both INSERT INTO worker_sessions statements now explicitly set claimed_at = now.to_rfc3339() instead of relying on the non-RFC3339 CURRENT_TIMESTAMP schema default. velocity.rs update_session_on_close() now parses defensively (RFC3339 first, falls back to SQLite native %Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S format, skips gracefully via Ok(false) instead of erroring if neither parses). cargo build --release clean, cargo test --release claim passes (2/2). Verified live: br close bf-atfo (previously failing with the exact reported error) now succeeds. Deployed to ~/.local/bin/bf on lab (old binary backed up to bf.pre-6af-fix.bak). Regression test not yet added to the test suite -- acceptance criteria 3 still open if you want a proper committed test, not just manual verification.

title: Fix overbroad Azure Key secret-scanner regex causing false positives on long paths
description:
src/secrets.rs:201 has: ("Azure Key", Regex::new(r"[a-zA-Z0-9/_-]{44}")?) — this matches ANY 44-char run of alnum/slash/dash/underscore with no surrounding-context requirement (every other built-in pattern requires a keyword like 'password', 'bearer', 'sk-', etc. nearby). This is the root cause of the fleet-wide known gotcha 'secret scanner false-positives on long absolute paths' (see this workspace's CLAUDE.md Beads section and reference_beads_no_direct_jsonl-adjacent memory). A typical scratchpad path like /home/coding/.tmp/claude-1000/-home-coding/<uuid>/scratchpad/... trivially contains a 44+ char alnum/slash/dash run and gets flagged as a secret, blocking legitimate bead bodies/comments that reference absolute paths.

Fix: tighten the Azure Key pattern to actual Azure storage account key shape (88 base64 chars, often ending in '==', frequently preceded by 'AccountKey=' or similar) or require a nearby keyword like other patterns do. Add a regression test in src/secrets.rs using a long absolute path fixture (e.g. the exact fleet-observed false-positive shape) asserting it does NOT trigger, alongside a still-passing true-positive Azure key fixture.

title: Fix assignee-clearing gap: bf create/update/reopen must never reject empty assignee
description:
Umbrella tracking bead for the assignee-clearing gap found during the 2026-07-21 lab NEEDLE fleet audit (see docs/plan/plan.md section 3.4 for full analysis).

The storage layer (src/storage/sqlite.rs update_issue) already correctly treats an empty/whitespace-only assignee as 'clear the field' (writes NULL). The CLI layer contradicts this: cmd_create and cmd_update both call validate_assignee() (src/validation.rs) which rejects empty/whitespace assignee with 'Assignee cannot be empty or whitespace-only', so the correct storage behavior is currently unreachable via the CLI. Separately, bf reopen never touches the assignee field at all, so reopened beads retain a stale foreign assignee.

This is not theoretical: it is confirmed live-blocking NEEDLE's bead-release-on-failure/timeout path and its new stale-assignee mend/self-heal step across a real multi-repo fleet on lab (100.81.129.38) as of 2026-07-21.

Closes when both child beads are closed and cargo test passes with the previously-ignored tests in tests/test_assignee_validation.rs restored and green.

Verified in tree: src/cli/mod.rs:13/1342/1613, src/validation.rs:38 (no validate_assignee left), tests/test_assignee_validation.rs has no #[ignore]/aspirational markers. cargo build clean; test_assignee_validation 12 passed 0 ignored; reopen regression tests (test_reopen_clears_assignee, test_reopen_without_assignee_is_noop) pass. title: Fix doctor --repair --flush-first write violation on healthy workspace
description:
The `bf doctor --repair --flush-first` command writes to JSONL even when the workspace is healthy and no repair is needed.

**Location:** doctor.rs lines 1007-1023

**Issue:** When `needs_rebuild` is false (healthy workspace), the function returns early at line 1003, but line 1011 still calls `storage.sync_to_jsonl(&jsonl_path, false)` if `opts.flush_first` is true.

**Impact:** A read-only diagnostic operation (repair that repairs nothing) performs a write to disk, violating the read-only contract.

**Reproduction:**
1. Create a healthy workspace with no corruption/divergence
2. Run `bf doctor --repair --flush-first`
3. Observe that JSONL is written even though no repair occurred

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] `bf doctor --repair` on a healthy workspace does NOT write to JSONL
- [ ] `bf doctor --repair --flush-first` on a healthy workspace does NOT write to JSONL (or documentation is updated to clarify this is expected behavior)
- [ ] All read-only commands have been audited and verified to have no write paths
- [ ] Tests added to prevent regression

title: NEEDLE mitosis still non-atomic: migrate bead-splitting to bf mitosis/bf batch (plan Phase 5.3 Race 3 unfixed)
description:
Plan gap audit (2026-07-19) against docs/plan/plan.md Phase 5.3 ("Race 3 -- Mitosis: create_bead + add_dependency") and this repo's own docs/needle-mitosis-migration.md guide.

bead-forge's whole reason for existing is eliminating race conditions in NEEDLE's bead operations. Two of the three documented races are already fixed and verified live: NEEDLE's bead_store/mod.rs run_bf_claim() (around line 555-895) calls `bf claim --assignee <actor> --json` for atomic select+claim, with a documented fallback to the old two-call br path only on error. That closes Race 1 and Race 2 from the plan.

Race 3 is NOT fixed. In ~/NEEDLE/src/bead_store/mod.rs, the `create_bead` (line ~753) and `add_dependency` (line ~776) trait methods each shell out separately via `run_br` (which execs the `bf` binary through the deprecated `br` compat shim): `create_bead` runs `br create --title ... --json --silent` and returns the new ID; `add_dependency` separately runs `br dep add <blocked> <blocker> --type blocks`. Whatever caller in NEEDLE splits a bead into children (create N child beads, link each as a blocker, then close the parent) still does this as N+N+1 sequential subprocess calls with no shared transaction. If NEEDLE is killed between these calls (SIGKILL, OOM, pod eviction -- all things that happen to fleet workers per this environment's operational history), you get an orphaned child bead with no dependency link, and the parent never closes. This is exactly the failure mode described in plan.md Phase 5.3 and is still live today.

bead-forge already ships the fix and has for some time: `bf mitosis <parent-id> --children '<json array>'` and the equivalent `bf batch` op sequence (src/batch.rs, tested in tests/batch_mitosis.rs) run the entire create-children + link-deps + close-parent sequence inside one SQLite BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction -- a kill -9 mid-operation leaves the workspace in its original state, verified by the crash-safety test in docs/needle-mitosis-migration.md.

Task: In the ~/NEEDLE repo (separate repo from bead-forge, on this same lab server), find the code path that orchestrates bead-splitting/mitosis (search for callers of `create_bead` combined with `add_dependency` for child-bead patterns -- it will NOT be named "mitosis" in NEEDLE's source, grep did not find that literal string, so look for the split/decompose logic in the strand or bead_store modules). Replace the N-call sequence with a single call to `bf mitosis` (or `bf batch` with the JSON op array), following the exact "Migration: One-line change in NEEDLE" section of ~/bead-forge/docs/needle-mitosis-migration.md, which includes a concrete before/after Rust code snippet. Keep the existing fallback-on-error pattern already used by run_bf_claim() (try bf, log+fall back to the old sequential calls on failure) so this degrades gracefully rather than becoming a hard dependency. Add or update a test in NEEDLE's own test suite proving no orphaned children survive a killed/failed mitosis call (mirror the verification steps in the migration guide). Run NEEDLE's normal test/lint gate before committing. This is a pure code change in a dev repo -- no secrets, no cluster/production access needed.

title: NEEDLE bf claim call omits --model/--harness/--harness-version, leaving velocity-aware scoring (plan 4B.6) dead
description:
Plan gap audit (2026-07-19) against docs/plan/plan.md section 4B.6 (Velocity-Aware Impact Scoring) and section 4.5 (CLI Usage), cross-checked against the live NEEDLE integration.

bead-forge fully implements velocity-aware claim scoring: the `worker_sessions` and `velocity_stats` tables exist (src/storage/schema.rs), `bf claim` accepts `--model`, `--harness`, `--harness-version` flags and folds them into the claim scoring query (src/claim.rs has a documented `velocity_adjusted_score` method and the plan's example CLI usage in section 4.5 is `bf claim --assignee worker-7 --model claude-sonnet-4-6 --harness needle --harness-version 0.5.2 --json`), and there is a `bf velocity` command to inspect the resulting table (src/cli/mod.rs `Commands::Velocity`).

However, the actual caller in ~/NEEDLE/src/bead_store/mod.rs (`run_bf_claim`, around line 555-590) invokes bf claim with only `["claim", "--assignee", actor, "--json"]` -- no --model, --harness, or --harness-version. Confirmed by direct grep of that function body. This means `worker_sessions` and `velocity_stats` in every live bead-forge workspace NEEDLE touches will stay empty (or only populated by whatever manually invokes bf claim outside NEEDLE), so the fleet never benefits from the "route beads to the model/harness combo that closes that issue_type fastest" behavior the plan calls out as a design decision (#14 in Key Design Decisions: "Worker composition is first-class metadata... The fleet becomes self-optimizing"). Right now it's a fully-built, fully-tested, dead feature from NEEDLE's side.

Task: In ~/NEEDLE (separate repo from bead-forge, same lab server), locate where the worker's model/harness/harness-version are already known at the call site of run_bf_claim (NEEDLE necessarily knows which model/harness config it launched, e.g. from its adapter config such as .config/needle/adapters/*.yaml mentioned in bead-forge's own plan.md migration checklist section, or from whatever context is passed into the pluck strand). Thread that metadata through to run_bf_claim and add `--model <value> --harness needle --harness-version <needle-version>` to the args vector before the existing `--assignee actor --json` args (do not change existing arg order/shape in a way that breaks the JSON parsing that follows). If any of the three values genuinely isn't available at that call site for some worker types, it's fine to omit that specific flag (bf claim's design already treats missing metadata as a documented fallback to the population-wide average, so partial metadata is safe, not an error). Add/update a NEEDLE test asserting the claim subprocess args include the expected flags when metadata is available. Run NEEDLE's normal test/lint gate before committing. Pure code change, no secrets, no cluster/production access.

title: blocked_issues_cache treats any non-closed/tombstone status (incl. completed) as still-blocking
description:
`bf update <id> --status completed` (or any tool/human writing status="completed") silently succeeds via Status::FromStr's catch-all Custom(String) variant (src/model.rs:108, "other => Ok(Self::Custom(other.to_string()))") -- there is no validation and no first-class Completed variant.

Root cause: is_terminal() (src/model.rs:73-75) only returns true for Closed/Tombstone. rebuild_blocked_cache() (src/storage/sqlite.rs:732-748) mirrors this exactly: "WHERE d.type IN ('blocks', 'parent-child', 'conditional-blocks', 'waits-for') AND i.status NOT IN ('closed', 'tombstone')" (line 742). A bead with status=completed looks done in bf list/bf show to a human, but the blocked-cache rebuild still counts it as an active blocker forever -- any dependent bead can never become ready via br ready, regardless of the deferred label or any other factor.

Confirmed at scale in production data across the lab NEEDLE fleet (2026-07-09): 106 beads across 15 of 22 audited repos currently have status=completed (vista 19, aide-de-camp 15, claude-print 12, claude-governor 11, gribtract 10, ARMOR 8, zai-proxy 6, NEEDLE 5, HOOP 5, ai-code-battle 5, drawrace 4, mobile-gaming 3, mta-my-way 1, AgentScribe 1, SIGIL 1) -- each one a potential permanent dependency-chain freeze, found via 'br list --status completed' in each workspace.

Acceptance criteria:
- Status::from_str (src/model.rs, ~line 108) rejects unrecognized status strings by default instead of silently accepting them as Custom(...), OR at minimum maps completed/done/finished to Status::Closed as explicit aliases -- pick whichever preserves br output-parity per this repo's CLAUDE.md (check what beads_rust/br itself does with unknown --status values before deciding).
- is_terminal() and the rebuild_blocked_cache() query's NOT IN (...) list are updated consistently with whatever the above decision is, so they can never drift apart again (ideally: is_terminal() becomes the single source of truth and the SQL query calls into or mirrors a shared constant, not a second hardcoded literal).
- Add a regression test: create bead A with status=completed, bead B that depends on/is blocked by A, rebuild_blocked_cache, assert B is NOT in blocked_issues_cache (or assert it currently IS, if the acceptance decision is instead to reject completed as an invalid status at write time -- either fix is acceptable as long as new completed-status beads cannot silently freeze dependents going forward).
- Write a `bf doctor` check (or extend an existing one) that finds and reports existing status=completed beads across a workspace, so the 106 already-affected beads found in production can be identified and migrated (to closed) without a manual per-repo sqlite query.
close_reason: Fixed. Design decision: checked beads_rust (the canonical br) and confirmed it ALSO allows arbitrary Custom status strings via the same catch-all FromStr pattern -- rejecting/aliasing at write time would break the documented br output-parity requirement, so Status::from_str is unchanged. Instead: Status::is_terminal() now also recognizes Custom("done")/Custom("completed") via a new TERMINAL_STATUS_ALIASES constant (model.rs); every one of the 11 SQL blocking-check sites that had drifted out of sync with each other (6 in claim.rs, 3 in storage/sqlite.rs, 2 in critical_path.rs -- some only checked closed, some checked closed+tombstone, none consistently) now use the same closed/tombstone/done/completed list, documented via a TERMINAL_STATUS_SQL_LIST comment convention so future changes are grep-able. Added bf doctor check (pseudo_terminal_status_ids) that surfaces any bead still sitting at a done-sounding non-canonical status, recommending bf close. Two regression tests added and passing: claim::tests::test_completed_status_blocker_unblocks_dependent, doctor::tests::test_check_reports_pseudo_terminal_statuses. Full suite: 103/104 pass (1 pre-existing unrelated environmental failure in sync::tests::test_find_workspace_not_found, documented in its own test comment as a TMPDIR quirk on this box). cargo build --release clean, deployed to ~/.local/bin/bf on lab (old binary backed up as bf.pre-bf-wre-fix.bak).

title: Add flush + git change detection to bf-checkpoint.sh
description:
Split slice #2 of parent bf-3cu1k (ADR-1 bf-checkpoint.sh). Depends on child bf-4gkg5 (config gating). The script already exists and is committed (fef0340) in deploy/ and scripts/. This child OWNS and VERIFIES only the flush + change-detection slice; sibling children own gating, commit, and throttle/push. Do NOT touch src/claim.rs or any claim/close hot path.

Scope (this slice only):
- git-repo preflight: `git -C "$WORKSPACE" rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree`; if not a repo, print a message and exit 0 (nothing to checkpoint).
- Step 1 flush: run `bf sync --flush-only -w "$WORKSPACE` BEFORE checking for the file (the JSONL is produced by the flush; checking pre-flush would bail on any never-flushed workspace).
- Step 2 detect change: `git diff --quiet -- .beads/issues.jsonl` for tracked changes AND `git status --porcelain -- .beads/issues.jsonl` to also catch a first-time untracked file (so the very first checkpoint lands).
- If the flush produced no issues.jsonl, OR there is no change, print a clear message and exit 0 WITHOUT committing.

Acceptance:
- On a clean workspace (jsonl unchanged after flush), the script flushes and exits 0 without staging/committing anything.
- A first-ever flush that creates a still-untracked issues.jsonl is detected as a change (not silently skipped).
- A non-git directory exits 0 with a 'not a git repository' message (no error, no commit).
- `bash -n` passes on both variants.
- src/claim.rs and any hot path UNTOUCHED.
close_reason: Verified slice #2 (flush + change detection) of parent bf-3cu1k. No source change: the script committed whole in fef0340 already implements git-repo preflight (exit 0 non-git), bf sync --flush-only BEFORE the file check, and change detection via 'git diff --quiet' + 'git status --porcelain' (catches first-ever untracked issues.jsonl). Verified end-to-end on isolated /tmp workspaces: clean workspace flushes and exits 0 staging/committing nothing (HEAD unchanged, index empty); first-ever flush creating still-untracked issues.jsonl is detected and committed (only .beads/issues.jsonl); non-git dir exits 0 with message. bash -n clean on both deploy/ and scripts/ variants. src/claim.rs and the claim/close hot path untouched (only src/format/* diffs vs HEAD, owned by other beads). Verification recorded in notes/bf-yrqmr.md (pushed on branch needle/bf-yrqmr).
